newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia energy minister sees fuel oil export tariff.
newsitem.headline: Russia energy minister sees fuel oil export tariff.

text.p: Russian Fuel and Energy Minister Pyotr Rodionov said on Thursday that Russia would introduce a tariff on heavy fuel oil (mazut) exports during the colder seasons, but would not impose any volume limits on shipments.
When asked if mazut exports would be curbed during the colder winter and spring seasons, he told Reuters in an interview, "We do not intend to introduce quotas, but we will introduce a tariff."
First Deputy Energy Minister Alexander Yevtushenko said at the end of August that Russia was considering an excise tax of possibly 14 European currency units (Ecus) per tonne on exports of mazut.

In December 1994, Russia suspended mazut exports, except those contracted under government supply programmes, to April 1995 to bolster domestic supplies during what it called the colder winter season.
Russia scrapped all energy export tariffs by July 1996 as part of a $10 billion, three-year loan agreement with the International Monetary Fund, but is now collecting duties on crude oil exports.
